images.title: Three bars, one average
images.purpose: Show how a statement about an average is tested: add the three yearly bars, then share the total equally.
images.composition: One group of three vertical bars centred in the frame on a plain baseline, a dashed levelling line across them, and one short caption line below; wide white margins on both sides.
exact_structure: Exactly 3 vertical bars of equal width standing on one grey (#6B7280) baseline, left to right labelled 2021, 2022, 2023 under the baseline.
Bar heights in the ratio 48 : 35 : 45, colours teal (#0072B2), amber (#E69F00), reddish purple (#CC79A7) left to right.
Each bar carries its value just above its top: 48, 35, 45.
One dashed grey (#6B7280) horizontal line across all three bars at height 42.7 on the same scale, so it is below the tops of the 48 and 45 bars and above the top of the 35 bar.
The part of the 48 and 45 bars above the dashed line is drawn with a light hatch, and the gap above the 35 bar up to the line is outlined, showing the extra filling the gap.
Below the bars, one caption line: Total 128, average 128 ÷ 3 ≈ 42.7.
No vertical axis, no gridlines, no organisation name.
rejection: a number of bars other than 3
the dashed line above the 48 bar or below the 35 bar
a total other than 128 or an average other than about 42.7
images.takeaway: An average of three bars is the level they reach when the total is shared equally, here about 42.7.
images.description: Three bars of heights 48, 35 and 45 with a dashed line at their average of about 42.7, and the total 128 below.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Point to the hatched tops filling the gap over the short bar before reading the caption.

image_decisions.why: A levelling picture shows what an average of three bar readings means when testing a statement.
